subject: Aurum Health - geozone erasure certification and SLA language
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@aurumhealth.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: legal@aurumhealth.com
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on geozone wipe/cert language in DPA v2

Hi Rafael —

Thanks for sending over the draft DPA. We reviewed section 4.2 and had a couple of follow-ups before we route to procurement/legal for signature:

1) Can Redwood provide an operational definition of "geozone wipe" vs "onshore delete"? Specifically, is the deletion window guaranteed or "best effort" for backups and snapshots?

2) For regulated data sets (PHI subset), we need a formal certificate of erasure within 30 days of request. Would you accept a 30-day certification SLT with a remediation credit for failures?

3) We saw the carveout for archived snapshots stored offline; can you share the retention schedule and whether those snapshots are included in on-demand erase requests?

We included a redline (attached) with proposed language that clarifies certifications and offers an audit point. Our legal prefers a deterministic timeline rather than "commercially reasonable efforts."

Appreciate a quick run-through so we can keep the procurement timeline unchanged.

Cheers,
Lena Ortiz
Head of Security & Compliance
Aurum Health

Attachment: aurum_redline_comments.pdf (review notes)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@aurumhealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 12:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on geozone wipe/cert language in DPA v2

Lena —

Thanks for the clear list. Looping in Monica (AE) and Marissa (Legal) — they'll drive scope and redlines from our side. Quick answers up front, then I'll follow with an internal playbook and a proposed amendment: 

1) Operational definitions: "Geozone wipe" = API-triggered logical deletion + background tombstoning + secure overwrite of ephemeral caches within the geozone; "Onshore delete" refers to lifecycle deletion for backups and snapshots that are stored in country-aligned storage pools. For backups/snapshots we operate a staged delete: tombstone immediately, physical overwrite per retention schedule (we can shorten for contractually-bound accounts).

2) Certificate timing: Redwood can provide an on-demand certificate of erasure. Standard is 45 days for full cylindrical proof across backups & cold snapshots; we can commit to 30 days for Aurum PHI with a limited SLA credit. Proposal: 30-day certificate for PHI with a 5% service credit if certificate issuance misses the window.

3) Archived snapshots: by default they are included in on-demand erasure requests but there are operational constraints if data is exported to tape/long-term vaults — we list those exceptions. We'll attach our scheduled_wipe_matrix and erasure_playbook for visibility.

I will attach a concise amendment we can add to the DPA and propose a one-page operational playbook that maps request -> trigger -> cert issuance -> audit artifacts. If that looks good, we can accept your redlines except the clauses that require third-party escrow for erasure verification — that will need legal sign-off.

Sending the materials now.

Best,
Rafael
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: erasure_playbook_v1.3.pdf, scheduled_wipe_matrix.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@aurumhealth.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on geozone wipe/cert language in DPA v2

Hi Lena —

Thanks for the annotated DPA. A few legal clarifications from our side on the items you flagged: 

- We can accept a deterministic 30-day certificate commitment for PHI, but need to limit the scope to data controlled within Redwood-managed storage in the contracted geozone (we cannot certify erasure for customer-managed on-prem copies or consumer backups taken out-of-band). We'll add a definition for "contracted geozone storage."

- The remediation mechanism: a fixed service credit (Rafael suggested 5%) is reasonable for single-incident miss. We cannot accept open-ended monetary penalty ladders — instead propose a tiered credit: 5% for first missed cert, 10% if multiple misses in a rolling 12 months.

- Auditability: we'll provide a certificate that contains the erasure playbook execution ID, list of storage object IDs (obfuscated) and a signed hash. For additional assurance, we can provide a SOC-style extract for the specific event at customer request (on paid audit retainer).

- Archive/tape: we will exclude customer-originated external backups and long-term export archives that are outside Redwood's custody. If Aurum requires those in scope, we need a connector plan and additional engineering charges.

I'll prepare a redline to the DPA that captures the accepted language and the items we need to carve out. If that looks OK to Aurum legal, we can route for signature.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Data & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redlined_DPA_Aurum_v2.pdf

From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@aurumhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: legal@aurumhealth.com, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Aug 2027 10:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on geozone wipe/cert language in DPA v2

Marissa —

Appreciate the quick turn. The high-level points look acceptable, but Aurum legal has two follow-ups before we sign: 

1) Can the 30-day certificate be triggered via API (programmatic request) and for it to return a unique reference ID we can store? We've included a note that the reference ID should be machine-verifiable so our incident ops can pull the certificate automatically.

2) For the proposed tiered credit, can the first missed cert be made a 7% credit (we are pushing to increase vendor skin in the game) or alternately add a short-term engineering SLA (e.g., priority M1 handling within 48 hours) as a remediation option?

We're close. If Redwood can support an API-triggered erase+cert with a machine reference ID and agree to consider the remediation alternative (engineering SLA) we'll accept the redline and proceed to procurement.

Thanks,
Lena

Attachment: aurum_redline_final_comments.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@aurumhealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on geozone wipe/cert language in DPA v2

Lena —

Following up after an engineering sync. Short answers:

- API trigger: yes. We'll expose an authenticated REST endpoint /v1/erasure-requests that returns an immutable request_id and status. Once the playbook completes we'll POST the certificate to the customer's webhook (if provided) and make the certificate retrievable via GET /v1/erasure-requests/{request_id}/certificate.

- Timing: we've re-baselined internal runbooks to support a 30-day cert for PHI when the request is flagged PHI and the account is under the "contracted geozone" flag. Ops will prioritize those jobs.

- Remediation: engineering SLA is a feasible alternative. We can offer: either 7% service credit for first missed certificate OR a guaranteed M1 engagement within 48 hours plus escalation to a named technical contact until closure (customer's choice). We will add the option into the DPA amendment.

Next steps: Marissa will incorporate the API reference ID and remediation options into the redline and we'll circulate final DPA. Rafael/Monica — can you confirm procurement timing?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Director, Platform Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: erasure_playbook_v1.3.pdf, scheduled_wipe_matrix.xlsx, redlined_DPA_Aurum_v2.pdf
